 2026 Media Guide Supplement (PDF)
 Head Coach Dabo Swinney will lead the Clemson Tigers into a game for the 250th time this Saturday when the Tigers face the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets on Saturday, Nov. 14. Kickoff at Memorial Stadium in Clemson, S.C. is set for 12:30 p.m. ET on The CW.
 On Oct. 18, 2008, Georgia Tech walked into Memorial Stadium in Clemson prepared to face the newly appointed interim Swinney in his first career game as head coach. 
 This week, more than 18 years later, the same opponent will walk in the same location to face Swinney as he completes his 250th career game as Clemson's head coach. Once he qualifies for the 250-game threshold on Saturday, Swinney's win total will be the third-highest by an FBS head coach through the first 250 games of a career.

 Opens in a new window WHAT TO WATCH FOR THIS WEEK
 Clemson attempting to earn its seventh win of the season and extend its streak of consecutive seven-win seasons to 16 years. Clemson would tie USC (2002- 17), Tennessee (1989-2004), Michigan (1968-83) and Georgia (2011-present) for the 17th-longest streak in the AP Poll era.
 Clemson and Georgia Tech facing one another for the 43rd of the last 44 years. By virtue of the ACC adopting a divisionless format with altered protected rivalries in 2023, the 2024 campaign marked the first year since 1982 that Clemson and Georgia Tech did not face one another.
 Head Coach Dabo Swinney coaching his 250th career game as Clemson’s head coach. 
 Swinney joining Frank Howard (295) as the only head coaches in school history to coach 250 career games.
 Swinney coaching his 250th career game to give him more games as a head coach than 145 of the 241 coaches inducted in the College Football Hall of Fame.
 Swinney (193) coaching his 250th career game to join Joe Paterno (212), Tom Osborne (212) and Bo Schembechler (190) as the only qualified coaches in FBS history to win 190 or more games in the first 250 games of a head coaching career.
 Swinney (193-56) attempting to pull within one win of Tom Osborne (195) for the most wins through the first 20 seasons of a head coaching career in FBS history. Notably, Swinney already ranks second in the category despite 2026 being his 19th season (and only his 18th full season).
 Swinney attempting to improve to 13-6 all-time against Georgia Tech, including postseason play. Georgia Tech is one of five schools against which Swinney has recorded at least a dozen career victories (Wake Forest, 16; Boston College, 15; NC State, 12; Florida State, 12).
